title: See that every story in a release reaches code
statement: As a developer, I can see that every story in a release reaches code through the Saga's links, so a release claims only work we can trace to something real.
overview: Trevor's direction: it is fine to have fixes with no story, as long as every story in a release has code references, and that should come from the transitive flow: stories belong to features, which have implementations, which link to code. That flow is the point of Change Saga, so nothing is linked by hand for this. On this Saga all 76 stories on built features reach code that way, while the Roadmap's reach none, which is the right answer for work not built yet. A path through a feature says the area has code, not that this story's part of it is built.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `release status` and the release's page name each of its stories that no recorded path connects to code.
A story reaches code through any recorded path: a slide Item linked to it or its criteria, a Task naming it, test evidence, or the implementation deck and test cases of the feature that holds it.
Each story shows the path it reached code by, so a story reached only through its feature reads differently from one linked directly.
A story with no path is shown and refuses nothing, at any point in a release.
An internal note marked as a fix, with no story, is not asked for code references.
